**WARN**

This is a Grok 4.6 high-effort read-only audit of the operating-plan bytes presented as digest `0d46bdb582174092f95ed4bcd454a3c6d4ce5e4fb28718e44e6598348eab2a80`. Requested identity: Grok 4.6, high effort. Returned identity: Grok 4.6 (xAI). Terminal state: audit complete. Digest was taken as given; it was not recomputed here. This is a vote on the workflow candidate only. It is not M3-D, M3-R, or M3-N, and it does not admit the MIL/3 draft or any implementation.

The plan correctly keeps S0 as funded AccrualFirst repay plus literal-fee transfer, separates design / local reference / native gates, repeats the U0 exit counts (66 absent embeddings, 0 covered K rows, 84 unenforced leaves), names Grok 4.6 high and GPT-6 Astra on the same full candidate, and records that no test, proof, compiler, or Preview run produced this text.

## Findings

1. **I1 is scheduled before the stage relation that I1 must implement.** Issue 3 says selecting exact `ProgramValid`, effect, footprint, head, authority, history, and retained-phase rules “Blocks reference and native implementation claims,” and requires positive and well-formed hostile traces for all six U0 judgments. Section 6 starts I1 after a D0 + signature/encoding packet. I1’s exit is a callable path that produces a canonical stage record and named rejections (wrong recipient, excess fee, missing funding, excess repayment, replay, incomplete transfer effects). Draft §4 still only *proposes* `Stage(...)`. Implementing `mil3-stage-v1.ts` against that unsettled relation recreates the current SP01.6 failure mode: stale binding and candidate inputs.

2. **The single active delivery item is still blocked SP01.6, and I1 is written so it can skip `cli.py run`.** Guarded status is SP01.6 loan-swap-subset, blocked on stale binding, missing current accounting, unavailable live resource state, and no pending transactions. The develop skill still requires one active item and registered dispatch through `cli.py run`. Section 1 says those facts block dependent dispatches and still allow “independently scoped source repair.” Section 4 adds that a “routine authorized source edit does not require a new campaign or design vote.” I1 is new S0 stage-preparation integration, including a new `experiments/moriarty-language/src/successor/mil3-stage-v1.ts` and `src/cli.ts` wiring. That work occupies the delivery slot already held by blocked SP01.6, and the exemption lets it proceed unregistered.

3. **I0 freezes a signature boundary that the same packet leaves unresolved.** I0’s deliverable is “freeze the S0 source/Core contract and its signature boundary.” Issue 1 still requires reconciliation of MIL/2 §11 with the U0 in-circuit proposal, plus valid and substituted-intent negative controls. Section 6’s first packet “records the unresolved MIL/2/U0 signature conflict.” A frozen signature boundary and an open conflict cannot both be true of the same I0 artifact. Local preparation can proceed with a named open Issue 1; a freeze cannot.

4. **M3-D and the first implementation step use different closed-issue sets.** M3-D requires every blocking row disposed: grammar, encoding, signature, numeric policy, failure relation, trust premises, migration, and the two full-candidate votes. The issue table treats rows 0–6 as that blocking set. Section 6 lets I1 start when two auditors agree on a supported S0 contract in the D0 + signature/encoding packet. Issues 2 (canonical encoding, unknown-tag rejection, `/2`→`/3` migration), 3 (stage/failure), 4 (numeric, including the U0 dust record versus MIL/3 residue), 5 (evidence/duties), and 6 (eight-family admission) remain outside that packet while I1 already consumes canonical stage records and S0 numeric/failure behavior.

5. **Implementer routing is unbound relative to the September 9 / `AGENTS.md` rule.** Startup routing is GPT-6 implementation plus fresh Grok 4.6 high and GPT-6 Astra audits. Section 2 binds those two auditors and forbids substituting a prior Opus review. Section 4 only says “the selected implementer.” The same section tells the lead to record routing conflicts before dispatch. Without a named implementer, dispatch can pick a convenient model for I1.

6. **“Freeze” is used without the U0-F / U0-S / U0-T label the plan itself requires.** Section 3 says the record must say which meaning of freeze it uses. I0 still says “Select and freeze the S0 source/Core contract.” U0 exit remains capability-open on embeddings, K coverage, pins, and native enforcement. An I0 freeze that is actually U0-F (contract text for the admitted S0 leaves, with absent leaves listed as fixed-empty) is coherent. An I0 freeze read as U0-S or U0-T is false on the recorded checkers: 1 present / 17 partial / 66 absent embeddings; 0 covered K rows; compatible tuple not established; 0/84 native-enforced leaves.

7. **Issue 4 and Issue 6 are written as blocking rows for work S0 cannot decide yet.** S0 is one signer/domain/asset, funded AccrualFirst repay, literal-fee transfer, no division or price. Issue 4 still bundles Ω placement, AMM fee placement, 23 B versus 21 B, vault bootstrap, and surplus. Issue 6 requires constructors and hostile pairs for all eight families before M3-D. Draft D1–D11 and §8.1 are specified-only follow-on profiles. Leaving 4 and 6 as blocking either stalls S0 on AMM/vault evidence or invites silent skip of rows the M3-D table still calls blocking.

8. **The I1 consumer path is specified well enough to audit later, and it is still only a proposal.** The required call is `createFinancialAgreementSourceV5().evaluate` on the Core/4 lifecycle path, with caller-proposed effects equal to the prepared result, and a transfer footprint covering both balances, sender allowance, replay state, work counters, and `ReadPre` / `NextWrite` / `Ensure` dependencies. That matches the startup fact that source/5 reaches Core/4 while `lower-compact.ts` still consumes an older path, and it matches draft §4’s complete derived footprint rule. The file `mil3-stage-v1.ts` is declared as a proposal, not an existing MIL/3 API. That honesty is sound; it does not make I1 eligible under findings 1–2.

## Required fixes

1. **Gate I0/I1 on Issue 0 and Issue 3, plus the S0 encoding subset of Issue 2.** Before any stage-preparation edit, freeze S0 `ProgramValid`, ExactEffects, FootprintSound (the full transfer footprint in §4 of this plan), HistoryLink, FailurePolicy, and the six-judgment positive/hostile pair. Keep AMM/vault/Ω/eight-family rows as named follow-on with owner and rejection rule. Record their status as non-blocking for S0 local preparation.

2. **Register S0 as the single active delivery item through guarded `cli.py run` after SP01.6 is parked, superseded, or left blocked without dependent edits.** Narrow the “routine authorized source edit” sentence so it cannot cover new successor files, `cli.ts` consumer wiring, or campaign-exempt I1. Keep the old loan/swap history immutable and unused as MIL/3 evidence until its accounting and bindings are reconciled.

3. **Split I0.** Version the S0 grammar, embedding map (every admitted leaf and every fixed-empty field among the 66 absences), and local stage examples as U0-F. Keep Issue 1 open for native signed acceptance. State in I0 that the wallet-signature scheme, signed bytes, digest, and verifier locus are unresolved, and that I1 may prepare unsigned local stages only.

4. **Name GPT-6 as implementer** for I1+ on this checkout, with Grok 4.6 high and GPT-6 Astra as the two full-candidate auditors. Record requested versus returned model identity on every dispatch. An absent reviewer supplies no vote.

5. **Rewrite the I1 start rule** to: two agreeing votes on the revised D0 packet (S0 slice, Issue 3 stage/failure, S0 encoding, open Issue 1) and a registered S0 delivery item. Agreement on this workflow document does not start I1.

6. **Label every later freeze** as U0-F, U0-S, or U0-T. M3-R stays closed until I2 has matching TypeScript/K acceptance, post-state, and error classification on the same corpus. M3-N stays closed while pins, certificates, and live resource state are unavailable.

Adopt this plan only after those edits. The current bytes are a usable skeleton for a read-only D0 decision packet. They are not authorization to implement MIL/3 or to treat DESIGN-MIL3-DRAFT.md as selected.
